A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTO research, despite the title and formatting changes. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on kidney and AAPM CT data, super-resolution results, runtime measurements, and padding and Fourier-transform ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, lung CT evaluation, distribution-shift tests, and additional controlled analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed CTO retains its spatial and frequency sinogram branches, averaged outputs, flipped circular padding, image-space DISCO operators, three reconstruction cascades, data consistency, and MSE objective. Expanded explanations and additional ablation configurations do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained kidney and AAPM datasets, v2 adds LIDC-IDRI lung CT evaluation, clean-training/noisy-testing conditions, kidney-to-AAPM transfer, and super-resolution with increased detector sampling. These substantially broaden the represented data and acquisition conditions. Nine-view evaluation already existed in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds MDPRNet, Learned Primal-Dual, LEARN, and RegFormer to the corresponding AAPM and kidney benchmark comparisons while retaining the original comparators. LEARN and RegFormer also join the super-resolution comparisons, and RegFormer is added to the runtime table.

E3.justification: v2 introduces single-rate versus joint-training controls, 72-view-trained baseline tests at other rates, a matched-parameter/FLOP control, and additional detector-resolution and noisy-input protocols. The reported training batch size changes from 16 in v1 Section 5.2 to 8 in v2 Appendix B.3; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Existing kidney/AAPM splits and reconstruction metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original padding and Fourier-axis ablations are retained. v2 adds removal of individual operators and sinogram branches, Bayesian hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, noise and cross-dataset robustness tests, single-rate training controls, and matched-capacity cost-versus-accuracy analysis. These investigate several previously untested explanations for CTO's performance.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table 6 newly report random-forest feature-importance estimates and Pearson correlations for the hyperparameter sweep. Existing plus/minus reporting is retained. Neither version specifies repeated-training run counts or seeds, and v2 adds no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original benchmark table values are retained after relocation, apart from equivalent rounding. v2 adds extensive comparator, control, robustness, and lung CT results: Appendix C.5 reports CTO advantages of 3.06 dB under noise and 9.8 dB under dataset transfer; Table 11 reports 31.11 versus 29.14 dB at matched capacity. The supplementary reconstruction figure also changes CNN/SART annotations from 31.08/26.71 to 31.80/26.75.

T1.justification: The reconstruction equations, Fourier-slice relationship, and Appendix A equivariance derivation remain unchanged. New Appendix D adds a secondary mathematical complexity analysis, specifying operator configurations and asymptotic costs for FNO, DISCO, LocalNO, and DeepONet, plus an argument about pre-discretized DISCO inference cost.

C1.justification: Beyond the retained sampling- and resolution-generalization claims, v2 adds headline claims of being the first neural-operator CT framework and strong robustness under dataset transfer and noisy measurements. These broaden the claimed novelty and applicability. The abstract's average CNN advantage changes from over 4 dB to over 3.4 dB, while the diffusion speedup claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of rate-specific overfitting, joint-training comparisons, and noise/transfer results as evidence of clinical robustness. Appendix D newly argues for DISCO's locality and efficiency relative to alternative operators and distinguishes matched-configuration costs from full CTO's additional computation. These explanations substantially extend v1's discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, detailed architectures and training settings for the new baselines, per-batch sampling-rate selection, hyperparameter-search procedures, exact parameter/FLOP counts, and inference kernel-caching information. The batch-size disclosure is also revised. These materially expand reproducibility information; actual online code availability was not verified.

R1.justification: The accelerated-CT discussion substantially expands, including LEARN, RegFormer, QN-Mixer, MDPRNet, and explicit positioning against Fan et al.'s multi-rate MVMS-RCN. New discussion distinguishes earlier multi-rate approaches from CTO's cross-resolution formulation and asserts first application of neural operators to sparse-view CT. Several earlier classical-reconstruction citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and experimental framing are extensively rewritten. AAPM replaces kidney CT as the main quantitative focus, existing analyses move between the main text and supplement, and the supplementary structure is reorganized. The title changes from Resolution-Independent to Resolution-Agnostic, with accompanying author and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, benchmark tables gain rows and method categories, AAPM and kidney tables exchange main/supplement placement, and Table 2 combines a new training-rate comparison with timing results. Additional analysis tables are introduced, while the existing supplementary figures are reordered and resized.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central performance claim. Tables 8 and 11 add training-regime and matched-capacity controls absent from v1's reported comparisons; the matched control retains a 31.11 versus 29.14 dB advantage with equal parameters and FLOPs. Broader baselines, component ablations, and robustness tests address important gaps in comparative evidence. New lung and transfer protocols remain briefly specified, and the batch-size revision is unexplained, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support and reproducibility disclosure.
